comparison: Both strongly support the core structural determination claims (C6-C8, C48-C50, C60-C63). OpenEval emphasizes the 3.2 Å resolution and RMSD comparison, while peer review highlights this as an 'important achievement' filling a gap in the elevator mechanism. Peer review also includes C105 (novelty claim) which OpenEval addresses separately in R11.

Both support the identification of conserved sodium binding sites (C9, C64-C71). OpenEval provides detailed structural justification with conservation across multiple structures, while peer review confirms 'they confirm the previously reported Na+ binding sites.' Peer review additionally includes C44 which OpenEval groups with R1.

Both evaluate the third metal-binding site as UNCERTAIN (C10, C72-C76). OpenEval notes conservative labeling and longer metal-ligand distances requiring additional biochemical characterization. Peer review similarly states the evidence is 'compelling' but 'not appropriate to model...without directly confirming experimentally.' Strong agreement on uncertainty. Peer review includes C45 which OpenEval groups with R1.

Both strongly support substrate binding site characterization and mutagenesis validation (C11-C13, C88-C89, C91-C96). OpenEval highlights differential effects of S300A vs S345A mutations, while peer review states 'the functional data is robust' and notes consistency with genetic assays. Strong agreement on functional validation. Peer review includes C87 which OpenEval addresses in R5.

Partial overlap with different emphases. OpenEval focuses on structural interactions and Neu5Gc accommodation inference (C14-C15, C87-C88, C97), while peer review addresses broader mechanistic implications and drug discovery potential (C14-C15, C86, C97-C99, C109). Both support the claims but peer review encompasses wider scope including druggability analysis that OpenEval addresses separately in R9 and R11.

Perfect claim overlap (C77-C80) but different evaluation types. OpenEval rates lipid modeling as UNCERTAIN, noting many densities are not well-defined and questioning functional significance of differential Lipid2 presence. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, with no specific concerns raised and implicit acceptance as part of overall structural quality. Disagreement on confidence level.

Perfect claim overlap (C81-C85) with full agreement. Both support the transport assay data. OpenEval highlights systematic design with appropriate controls, while peer review states 'the functional data is robust.' Strong concordance on functional validation experiments.

Perfect claim overlap (C51-C59) with full agreement. Both support domain architecture and structural comparison claims. OpenEval details connecting helix redundancy and conservation analysis, while peer review affirms structural quality and convincing structural analysis. Strong concordance.

Strong overlap (C100-C104, C106-C108) with agreement on SiaP vs SiaQM comparative binding analysis. OpenEval emphasizes structural comparisons and computational druggability analysis (C86, C98-C99), while peer review notes 'appropriately careful interpretations' and acceptance of comparative binding properties. Both support the differential affinity inferences.

OpenEval evaluates detergent screening and SEC methodology (C46-C47) as supported standard methodology. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though these technical details are implicitly accepted as part of overall structural quality assessment.

OpenEval addresses novelty claim (C105) and implications/limitations (C109) separately. Peer review incorporates C105 into the core structural determination evaluation (R1) and C109 into mechanistic implications (R5). Both support these claims but organize them differently in their evaluations.
